MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

This mutual non-disclosure agreement is entered into between ExampleCorp Ltd, a company incorporated in England and Wales, and Havenbrook Media, a company incorporated in England and Wales. Each is referred to individually as a party and together as the parties.

1. Parties

This mutual non-disclosure agreement is made between the two parties identified in the signature block, each a party and together the parties. The parties wish to exchange certain confidential information in connection with discussions about a potential commercial relationship in the media services sector, and this agreement records the terms on which that information will be disclosed and protected.

2. Definitions

Confidential Information means any information disclosed by one party to the other, in any form, that is marked as confidential or that would reasonably be regarded as confidential given its nature and the circumstances of disclosure. Confidential Information includes, without limitation, business plans, financial information, product roadmaps, technical data, customer lists, and the fact that discussions between the parties are taking place. Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes public through no breach of this agreement, that was already lawfully known to the receiving party free of any duty of confidence, that is received from a third party entitled to disclose it, or that is independently developed without use of the disclosing party's Confidential Information.

3. Confidentiality obligations

Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information strictly confidential, shall use it solely for the purpose of evaluating a potential business relationship, and shall protect it with at least the same care it applies to its own confidential information, and in any event with no less than reasonable care. Neither party shall copy, reproduce, or reverse engineer any Confidential Information except to the extent reasonably necessary for the permitted purpose.

4. Permitted disclosures

A party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, professional advisers, and affiliates who need to know it for the permitted purpose and who are bound by obligations at least as protective as those in this agreement. A party may also disclose Confidential Information where required by law, regulation, or a court of competent jurisdiction, provided it gives the other party prompt written notice where lawful, so that the other party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. The receiving party remains responsible for any act or omission by its representatives that would constitute a breach of this agreement if committed by the receiving party itself.

5. Term

This agreement takes effect on the date of the last signature and continues for two (2) years unless terminated earlier in accordance with its terms. The expiry of this agreement does not affect any Confidential Information disclosed while it was in force, which remains subject to the obligations set out in this agreement for the survival period described below.

6. Termination

Either party may terminate this agreement by giving forty-five (45) days' written notice to the other party. Termination does not affect rights or obligations accrued before the termination date, and the confidentiality obligations survive for three (3) years after termination.

7. Return or destruction

On the other party's written request, each party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of that party in its possession or control and, if requested, certify the destruction in writing. A party may retain copies required by law, regulation, or its bona fide internal compliance policies, provided those copies remain subject to the confidentiality obligations in this agreement for as long as they are retained.

8. Limitation of liability

Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, each party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this agreement shall be uncapped, and no financial limit shall apply to any loss, damage, cost, or claim, howsoever arising. Nothing in this agreement excludes or limits either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for any other liability that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited.

9. Governing law

This agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising from it, including any dispute relating to its existence, validity, or termination.

10. Notices

Notices under this agreement must be in writing and are effective when delivered to the registered office of the receiving party, marked for the attention of its legal counsel. Notices may be delivered by hand, by pre-paid first-class post, or by email, and are deemed received on the date of delivery if delivered by hand or email, or three business days after posting if delivered by post.

11. General

This agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties regarding its subject matter, supersedes all prior discussions, and may only be amended in writing signed by both parties. No failure or delay in exercising any right under this agreement operates as a waiver of that right. If any provision of this agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force and effect. Neither party may assign or transfer its rights or obligations under this agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. This agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and which together form one instrument.

Signed by the duly authorised representatives of the parties.
